title: Compounding of offences - which cases can genuinely be settled
p1:
Not every criminal case has to end with a long courtroom battle.

But here is the surprising part: some offences can legally be settled between the accused and the victim, while others cannot be closed just because both sides agree.
p2:
Many people think that if a complainant withdraws the case, the matter automatically ends. That is not true.

Compounding of offences means a legal settlement where the law allows the victim and accused to resolve certain offences, usually those involving private disputes. The permission depends on the nature of the offence and the applicable legal provisions.
p3:
For example, some minor offences involving personal disputes may be compoundable, while serious offences affecting society generally cannot be settled privately. The key question is not only 'Do both parties want to settle?' but also 'Does the law permit settlement for this offence?'

Knowing this difference can save time, money, and unrealistic expectations when handling a legal dispute.
conclusion: Have you ever assumed that withdrawing a complaint automatically closes a criminal case? What was your understanding of compounding of offences before reading this?
